_comment: Curated seeds for the software domain. build_catalog.py --domain software reads this file, asks GitHub for each repository's license, language, stars and last push, and writes software/. Edit the seeds here and rebuild; never hand-edit the generated files. Each seed: name, url, category, why (one line on why it is useful, written for this catalog; some stay close to the project's own description). Optional listed_in: a page in this repository that already lists the repository (for example catalog/engines.md); the seed is then linked from its category page instead of listed twice, and the build stops if that page no longer lists it.
title: Software
intro: Open-source applications, tools, libraries and curated lists beyond games: self-hosting, home automation, local AI, documents, media, notes, reading, learning, personal finance, privacy and web development.

Each row is a hand-picked project with one line on why it is useful. Its license, language, stars and last push are read from GitHub's API when the list is built, and its reuse class follows the same [license rule](../README.md#the-license-rule) as the games catalog. Rows are chosen for being maintained and widely used, not for completeness; the [resources](#resources) below go wider.

**Anything you install runs code on your machine.** Prefer a project's own releases or an official package, pin a version, read what access it asks for, and keep services that hold your data off the open internet unless you mean to publish them. **A code license says nothing about model weights, voices, fonts, art or data**, which often carry their own terms. This is practical guidance, not legal advice.

categories.title: Self-hosting
categories.scope: servers, reverse proxies, remote access, monitoring and household apps you run yourself

categories.title: Home automation
categories.scope: hubs, device bridges, cameras and automations that run locally

categories.title: Local AI and agents
categories.scope: model runners and servers, coding agents, agent frameworks and evaluation
categories.note: Agents run code and edit files with your access. Read the code, pin a version and give them the least access that works; the [safe setup checklist](../../ai/graphics.md#safe-setup-checklist) applies. A code license says nothing about model weights; read each model card.

categories.title: Agent memory
categories.scope: memory layers, knowledge graphs and context stores that keep what an agent learned across sessions
categories.note: A memory layer stores what your agents read and say. Most send that text to a hosted model for extraction and embeddings by default, and several send usage telemetry; set local models and turn telemetry off before adding private data. The [safe setup checklist](../../ai/graphics.md#safe-setup-checklist) applies.

categories.title: MCP servers and SDKs
categories.scope: Model Context Protocol servers, SDKs, gateways and debuggers that connect AI tools to other software
categories.note: **Every MCP server runs code on your machine with the access you give it.** Read the code, pin a version, keep it local, and apply the [safe setup checklist](../../ai/graphics.md#safe-setup-checklist) before connecting one to an agent.

categories.title: Agent skills and instruction files
categories.scope: instruction files, skills and plugins that change how a coding agent works
categories.note: A skill is instructions your agent follows with your access, and some plugins add hooks that run at every session start. Read it before installing, install from a reviewed commit rather than a branch, and check each skill's license: one repository can mix licenses. The [safe setup checklist](../../ai/graphics.md#safe-setup-checklist) applies.

categories.title: Speech
categories.scope: speech-to-text and text-to-speech that run locally
categories.note: A code license says nothing about model weights or voices, which often carry their own terms; read each model card. Clone a voice only with its owner's consent.
